rationale: The validation report contains issue 'golden_rejected': evaluate.py rejects the golden correct solution (exit_code 1) when it must PASS. The golden implements exactly the pinned interface: synchronous write/reset in an always @(posedge clk) block updating an internal 4x8 register array, with rdata0/rdata1 as pure combinational assigns of that array indexed by raddr0/raddr1. This is a fully compliant, well-formed word-level implementation of the pinned port list and timing contract. The failure signature is not a cycle-offset/timing-shape disagreement between two independently authored designs (which would indicate a specification defect) -- it is an internal testbench defect: the diagnostic 'missing PROBE for cycle 0' on FR1/FR3/FR4 for the golden run, combined with the analyzer's finding that tb_regfile.v has a declaration-order/race issue between a stimulus-file-loading initial block and a driving initial block (both synchronized only by a bare #1 delay), indicates the testbench itself is failing to emit or capture probe data at cycle 0 due to a race/synchronization bug in evaluation/tb_regfile.v, not because the golden design's waveform is offset by a fixed number of cycles from a differently-timed reference. The repeated identical failure signature across two attempts confirms this is a persistent harness bug, not a flaky timing race. Because mutation_baseline_run correctly did not run (blocked_by_differential) and mutation_score is not meaningful, and discrimination_coverage is 0.0, this case must be sent back to repair the evaluation harness rather than retained.
revision_instructions: In evaluation/tb_regfile.v, fix the stimulus-loading and drive-sequencing race that causes PROBE data to go missing for cycle 0 on FR1, FR3, and FR4 even for a correct, spec-compliant submission. Concretely: (1) declare all regs (including the plusargs-target reg used to hold the stimulus filename) before any initial block references them; (2) do not rely on two independent initial blocks synchronized only by a bare '#1' delay to sequence 'load stimulus arrays from file' before 'drive DUT with those arrays starting at cycle 0' -- merge the file-loading and DUT-driving logic into a single initial block with sequential blocking statements (or use a named event that the driving block explicitly waits on) so stimulus arrays are guaranteed fully populated before cycle 0 is driven or probed. (3) Re-verify that all requirement checks (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR3) grade the submission behaviorally by compiling and simulating it against this testbench through the pinned interface (clk, rst, we, waddr, wdata, raddr0, raddr1, rdata0, rdata1) and observing produced waveforms -- never by matching source text or structure. (4) After the fix, confirm the golden submission (a synchronous-write, combinational-read implementation obeying the pinned timing contract: write-then-read-forwarding with no extra latency, synchronous reset clearing all entries visible from the next edge, and fully independent read ports) passes all seven requirements with exit code 0, and that the naive baseline (which ties rdata0/rdata1 to constant zero) still fails as expected. (5) Additionally implement explicit numeric reporting of the four declared metrics (cycle_accurate_match_rate, word_recovery_rate, structural_match_accuracy, functional_equivalence) as fractions in evaluate.py's output, not just per-requirement PASS/FAIL booleans, so metric-level scoring aligns with the task specification's evaluation.metrics section.
